The Operations Manager is expected to continuously identify opportunities to improve profitability, service delivery, productivity, guest satisfaction, online reputation, hygiene, food safety, and sustainability performance. Maintain a strong operational presence throughout the hotel, particularly during peak periods, major events, high occupancy, VIP arrivals, and high-volume Food & Beverage operations. Work closely with department heads to identify operational challenges, service gaps, productivity opportunities, and areas requiring corrective action. Regularly review operating procedures, service flows, staffing deployment, opening and closing routines, guest touchpoints, and departmental processes to improve efficiency and productivity. Lead structured operational reviews and ensure agreed actions are implemented, monitored, and sustained. Conduct regular hotel inspections, operational walk-throughs, back-of-house inspections, and public area reviews to ensure presentation, cleanliness, maintenance, safety, and service standards are consistently achieved. Coordinate closely with Engineering, Housekeeping, Security, Front Office, Food & Beverage, Culinary, Sales, and other departments to resolve operational issues affecting the guest experience. Provide operational leadership across restaurants, bars, lounges, in-room dining, banqueting, catering, and other Food & Beverage outlets. Ensure Food & Beverage operations consistently deliver strong guest experiences while achieving budgeted revenue, profitability, productivity, and cost-control objectives. Work with Food & Beverage and Culinary leadership to optimize menus, concepts, service delivery, operating hours, promotions, average spend, covers, table utilization, and overall outlet performance. Monitor Food & Beverage cost of sales, payroll productivity, wastage, breakage, complimentary consumption, inventory controls, and other key cost drivers. Identify opportunities to increase outlet profitability through improved revenue generation, upselling, cost management, operational efficiency, and resource allocation. Ensure service standards, product quality, presentation, speed of service, ambience, and colleague engagement remain consistently high across all Food & Beverage operations. Oversee the operational execution of banquets, meetings, conferences, weddings, social functions, and major hotel events. Ensure close coordination between Service, Culinary, Sales, Engineering, Security, Stewarding, and other supporting departments. Review major event requirements, function sheets, operational plans, staffing levels, guest flows, set-up requirements, service timelines, and contingency arrangements. Ensure events are delivered professionally, efficiently, safely, and in accordance with client expectations, contractual requirements, and hotel standards. Support the optimization of banquet and event profitability through effective labour planning, resource utilization, equipment management, food cost controls, and operational productivity. Personally oversee significant events and high-profile functions where senior operational leadership is required. Maintain high visibility throughout guest areas and proactively engage with guests to understand their experience and identify opportunities for improvement. Ensure guest complaints, service failures, and operational concerns are handled promptly, professionally, and with appropriate service recovery. Review guest satisfaction results, online reviews, social media feedback, brand quality scores, and other reputation indicators on a regular basis. Monitor online guest review platforms and identify recurring themes affecting service, product quality, cleanliness, Food & Beverage, facilities, or overall guest satisfaction. Work with department heads to establish corrective action plans addressing negative trends and recurring guest concerns. Ensure positive guest feedback and best practices are shared with teams to reinforce desired service behaviours. Drive measurable improvement in guest satisfaction scores, online reputation ratings, review sentiment, and overall guest loyalty. Support the General Manager in delivering the hotel's annual revenue, profitability, GOP, payroll, productivity, and operating cost objectives. Participate in the preparation and ongoing management of operating budgets, forecasts, manning plans, departmental expenses, and capital requirements. Regularly review departmental financial performance and identify opportunities to improve revenue, control costs, reduce wastage, and increase profitability. Ensure staffing levels and deployment are aligned with occupancy, Food & Beverage demand, event activity, seasonality, and business volumes. Challenge inefficient operating practices and unnecessary expenditure while ensuring cost-saving initiatives do not negatively affect guest experience, safety, or brand standards. Support revenue-generating initiatives across Rooms, Food & Beverage, Banqueting, Events, and other hotel operations. Develop a strong commercial culture among operational leaders, ensuring managers understand the financial impact of operational decisions. Continuously evaluate hotel operating models, staffing structures, processes, technology, and resource utilization to identify productivity opportunities. Monitor departmental productivity indicators including payroll percentage, hours per occupied room, covers per labour hour, revenue per colleague, overtime, casual labour utilization, and other relevant operational metrics. Ensure departmental scheduling reflects business demand and promotes effective utilization of permanent, casual, outsourced, and temporary resources. Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce duplication, improve communication, optimize workflow, and improve service delivery. Support the implementation of operational technology and systems that improve productivity, guest convenience, service consistency, reporting, and management control. Ensure the hotel maintains consistently high standards of food safety, hygiene, sanitation, and cleanliness throughout all Food & Beverage and back-of-house areas. Ensure compliance with HACCP principles, local food safety regulations, company standards, and applicable health authority requirements. Work closely with Culinary, Food & Beverage, Stewarding, Hygiene, Engineering, and other relevant teams to ensure proper food handling, storage, preparation, temperature control, cleaning, waste management, and sanitation procedures. Conduct regular hygiene and food safety inspections and ensure any deficiencies are addressed immediately. Ensure appropriate corrective and preventive actions are implemented following food safety or hygiene concerns. Promote a strong culture of food safety and hygiene accountability across operational departments. Champion the hotel's sustainability objectives and ensure environmental considerations are embedded within daily operations. Identify opportunities to reduce food waste, energy consumption, water consumption, single-use materials, chemicals, and unnecessary operating waste. Support responsible sourcing, recycling, waste segregation, sustainable Food & Beverage practices, and environmentally responsible operational procedures. Work with Culinary and Food & Beverage teams to monitor and reduce food waste without compromising product quality or guest satisfaction. Support sustainability reporting, audits, certifications, and company environmental initiatives. Engage colleagues and operational leaders in practical sustainability initiatives that generate measurable environmental and financial benefits. Ensure hotel operations comply with all applicable health, safety, fire, security, emergency, and operational policies and procedures. Ensure emergency procedures are understood, regularly reviewed, and appropriately implemented by operational teams. Work closely with Security and Engineering to maintain a safe and secure environment for guests, colleagues, contractors, suppliers, and visitors. Immediately escalate significant operational, safety, hygiene, food safety, security, or reputational risks to the General Manager. Lead operational teams with a strong focus on accountability, collaboration, service excellence, and commercial performance. Set clear performance expectations and ensure departmental leaders establish measurable objectives aligned with hotel priorities. Coach and develop operational leaders to strengthen their commercial awareness, leadership capability, guest focus, and operational discipline. Promote effective communication between departments and ensure teams are kept informed of business priorities, operational changes, guest feedback, events, and performance expectations. Support succession planning and the development of high-potential colleagues within operational departments. Foster a working environment where colleagues are encouraged to identify improvements, solve operational problems, and take ownership of the guest experience.

review_candidates.title: National Knowledge and Learning Officer
review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates as well as external women candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope This position is based in Erbil and will support IOM Iraq’s Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) efforts across all programmes (humanitarian and development). Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Chief of Mission and direct supervision of the Monitoring & Reporting Officer, the National Knowledge and Learning Officer will support the mission’s approach to institutional learning and knowledge-sharing. With IOM Iraq’s broad portfolio across durable solution, peace building and stabilization, migration management, migration health and emergency response, there is a critical need to capture lessons learned, evaluate outcomes, and foster continuous improvement. The incumbent will implement systems to manage knowledge generated by projects (evaluations, research, best practices) and to inform strategic planning. The role is embedded in the mission’s MEAL Unit and works closely with programme teams, PSU, Research Team, the Regional M&E Officer, and external evaluation partners. Responsibilities Contribute to establishing, and monitoring a mission-wide Knowledge and Learning Management (KLM) system for IOM Iraq. This includes maintaining appropriate tools and platforms (e.g. knowledge repositories, lessons learned and management response database) to systematically capture, store, and disseminate programmatic lessons, research findings, evaluations, and best practices. Contribute to making the system user-friendly, accessible across the mission, and aligned with donor commitments and IOM requirements. Plan, and coordinate programme and project evaluations in accordance with IOM’s Evaluation Policy and donor requirements. I Implement an annual evaluation and lessons learned workplan; coordinate independent external evaluations, including drafting Terms of Reference, liaising with IOM’s Evaluation Unit as required, procuring evaluation consultants or firms, and providing necessary data and documentation. Review inception and final reports to verify quality, compliance with standards, and usability of findings before final approval by the supervisor. Coordinate mission-wide research initiatives and formative studies to inform programme design and adaptive management. Work with programme teams to identify knowledge gaps and learning needs, and coordinate studies such as needs assessments, outcome and process evaluations, case studies, after-action reviews, and lessons-learned exercises. Verify methodological rigor, ethical compliance, and proper documentation of findings. Support the supervisor in transforming data, research, and evaluation findings into actionable learning to improve programme quality. Support the M&E Officer in organizing and facilitating learning events, including evaluation debriefs, project review meetings, brown-bag sessions, learning workshops, and annual programme reviews. Contribute to the development of concise learning products such as briefs, success stories, presentations, and recommendations to support evidence-based decision-making. Provide technical guidance and training on evaluation and learning to IOM staff and partners. Support programme teams in developing Monitoring and Evaluation frameworks and learning plans; train focal points on documenting best practices and lessons learned; and train national M&E staff in survey design, data analysis, reporting, and facilitation of learning discussions. Contribute to a mission-wide culture of knowledge-sharing and continuous learning. Support internal and external knowledge exchange practices coordination and engagement with the Regional M&E Officer, other IOM missions, and inter-agency M&E or knowledge management working groups to share best practices and align with UN system learning initiatives. Collaborate with government counterparts, donors, academic institutions, and other stakeholders to integrate feedback and disseminate IOM learning externally when appropriate. Contribute to the integration of cross-cutting themes (Protection, Gender, Accountability to Affected People) across all evaluation, research, and learning activities. Contribute to donor and internal reports by providing analysis of lessons learned, evidence of adaptive management, and programme improvements. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of IOM evaluation, monitoring, and Results-Based Management (RBM) frameworks, tools, and institutional requirements. Comply with IOM strategies, policies, and planning frameworks, and provide technical support to strengthen mission adherence. Implement knowledge and learning management plan, methods and tools on all projects and programmes, and collect, analyse, and report on lessons learned, project review meeting, success stories, internal and external evaluations in accordance with donor commitments and IOM requirements. Support in organizing and facilitating learning workshops, project review meetings, evaluation validation workshops, community of practice exercises, and collate and document best practices to share with the wider community in the IOM network and partners. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master’s degree in social sciences, development studies, evaluation, organizational learning, international relations, monitoring and evaluation, statistics, antropology, law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution ; or University degree in the above fields with two years of relevant professional experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), research, or knowledge management in humanitarian or development programmes. Experience in an international organization or UN agency is preferred. Demonstrated experience in designing or managing evaluations-including developing TORs, coordinating with evaluators, and disseminating results. Familiarity with both qualitative and quantitative evaluation methods and standards (e.g. OECD/DAC evaluation criteria) is required. Proven experience in facilitating organizational learning: organizing workshops, after-action reviews, or communities of practice to reflect on project performance and outcomes is required. Excellent writing and reporting skills - able to synthesize technical evaluation findings into clear, concise reports and presentations. Experience authoring evaluation reports or research publications is a strong advantage. Experience in designing or managing knowledge/information systems or databases for capturing lessons and best practices is an advantage. Skills Analytical skills: Ability to analyze complex project data and outcomes, and identify patterns, successes and areas for improvement. Should be comfortable working with statistical data as well as qualitative information. Knowledge of evaluation methodologies: Familiarity with logical frameworks, theory of change, survey design, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, etc., and ability to guide others in these techniques. Communication and facilitation: Strong ability to communicate technical information to diverse audiences; skilled in facilitating discussions and learning events with staff at different levels. Project management: Excellent organizational skills to manage multiple evaluations or studies simultaneously, ensuring timely delivery. Capable of managing external consultants and coordinating stakeholders. Technological literacy: Proficient in MS Office; knowledge of data analysis software (e.g. SPSS, R) or visualization tools is an asset. Comfortable with collaborative tools (SharePoint, Teams) for knowledge sharing. Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills; and, Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with people of diverse cultural and national backgrounds. Expert knowledge of MS office and advanced statistical skills including knowledge of database management, statistical and project management software is a strong advantage; Knowledge and understanding of the migration issues, return and reintegration in the region is an advantage. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). For this position, Fluency in English is required Arabic and Kurdish are advantage Languages Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies
